sections.h2: Selling a house in Englewood, NJ
sections.html:
Englewood is a small Bergen County city of 4.93 square miles with 30,035 residents, and it enforces a Certificate of Continued Occupancy on every sale of a one, two or multi-family house. The inspection is short, but the permit check that comes first can take longer than the visit itself, so begin early.

The median owner-occupied home is valued at $544,100, median household income is $102,571, and 54.5 percent of homes are owner occupied. The city has 11,274 households.

sections.h2: How the Certificate of Continued Occupancy works
sections.html:
City Ordinance 85-40, in Chapter 9 of the Revised General Ordinances, says a seller must receive a CCO before ownership transfers. New construction and buildings the state inspects, such as hotels and rooming houses, are outside it. The point is to check safety and to hand the new owner information about fire and occupancy rules.

  1. Once you have a buyer, the seller or agent visits the Englewood Municipal Building at 2-10 North Van Brunt Street, second floor, and tells the Building Department about the sale.
  2. Any open permits for work on the property must be closed out before an inspection can be scheduled.
  3. The application asks for the property address, owner and buyer contact details, the buyer's present address (or a mailing address for an LLC or corporation), and the number of people living there before and after the sale.
  4. You pay the fee to the City of Englewood and the inspector visits.
  5. The certificate is passed to the buyer at closing.

Selling without a CCO risks fines and delays at the closing table. The application asks about occupancy before and after the sale, so have the buyer's details ready when you go in, and keep a copy of the receipt for the fee. If the buyer is an LLC or corporation, bring its mailing address instead of a home address.

Englewood CCO fees and what the inspector checks
Fee or checkRequirement
Fee, one or two family house$150
Fee, multi-family building$250
StructureWalls, floors, ceilings, stairs and rails intact and safe
Smoke detectorAt least one working unit on each level of living space
Carbon monoxide detectorAt least one working unit within 10 feet of each bedroom
Fire extinguisherOne ABC type, 2 to 10 pounds, within 10 feet of each kitchen

The same visit looks for illegal installations, illegal apartments and illegally rented rooms.

sections.h2: What if the inspector finds an illegal unit or unpermitted work?
sections.html:
The owner has to remove the extra unit, which means cutting off utility service and removing the added kitchen and bathroom. The certificate issues only after a second inspection confirms the work is done and the code is met. Work that needed a permit and did not get one must go through the Building Department first.

If you suspect an old basement apartment or an attic conversion has no paperwork, talk to the Building Department before you accept a contract. Raising it early leaves time to renegotiate before the closing date is fixed. Buyers rarely walk away from a clearly explained problem, but they do from a surprise at the inspection.

Median selected monthly owner costs are $3,464 with a mortgage and $1,500 or more without one, and median gross rent is $1,977. Englewood borders Bergenfield, Englewood Cliffs, Fort Lee, Leonia, Teaneck and Tenafly, and Highwood is an unincorporated community inside its lines. Street names such as Brinckerhoff, Van Brunt, Lydecker, Demarest and Van Nostrand recall the early families, and houses on Grand Avenue include several of the city's National Register sites.

Flat Rock Brook is a 150 acre preserve on Van Nostrand Avenue with 3.6 miles of trails, and MacKay Park on North Van Brunt Street has a pool, rink and athletic fields. Mention whichever is closest in your listing, along with the walk or drive to the bus stop, since commuters and families both read for that.

Compare your carrying costs against these medians when deciding how long to wait for an offer. An inherited house with a mortgage-free balance costs far less to hold than one carrying a payment, which changes how patient you can afford to be.

Interstate 95 clips the city for 0.43 miles near the Leonia line. Routes 4 and 93 and county routes 501 and 505 carry local traffic. NJ Transit bus 166 runs to the Port Authority Bus Terminal, while routes 171, 175, 178 and 186 serve the George Washington Bridge Bus Station, and Rockland Coaches also runs to Port Authority. Mean travel time to work is 30.9 minutes, so a listing that states the nearest bus line helps buyers who work in Manhattan.

The Englewood Public School District runs five schools, from the D. A. Quarles Early Childhood Center to Dwight Morrow High School, which also takes students from Englewood Cliffs. Bergen County students can apply to the Bergen County Academies and other county technical programs.

sections.h2: State fees at the deed and where it is recorded
sections.html:
Bergen County's Clerk acts as the recording officer for deeds, mortgages and liens. The state charges the seller a realty transfer fee on the deed, and any price above $350,000 uses a higher schedule: for example, $4.80 per $500 on the slice between $200,000 and $550,000. Sales above $1,000,000 add a graduated percent fee that starts at 1 percent.

A resident seller signs the state's GIT/REP-3 form for recording, and nonresident sellers use GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 unless a stated assurance applies. For a tax assessment challenge, the county board of taxation must receive your petition by April 1, or May 1 where a revaluation or reassessment took place.

Once a buyer is lined up, call the Building Department the same week. Ask whether any permit from past work is still open, close it out, and only then request the inspection. While you wait, test every smoke and carbon monoxide detector, put an ABC extinguisher of 2 to 10 pounds within 10 feet of each kitchen, and walk the stairs and railings for anything loose.

A cash buyer does not avoid the CCO. The ordinance applies whenever ownership changes hands, so the buyer's attorney will ask for the certificate at closing, and a missing one can push the closing date back. A cash sale does save you the lender's appraisal and the repair negotiations that often follow a mortgage buyer's inspection. If the house has a basement apartment or attic room, tell the buyer up front and fix the paperwork or remove the unit before the inspector arrives.

faqs.q: Do I need a CCO to sell a house in Englewood?
faqs.a: Yes. City Ordinance 85-40 requires a Certificate of Continued Occupancy for one, two and multi-family houses before ownership changes hands.

faqs.q: How much is the Englewood CCO inspection?
faqs.a: $150 for a one or two family home and $250 for a multi-family building, paid to the City of Englewood with the application.

faqs.q: What does the Englewood inspector look at for fire safety?
faqs.a: A working smoke detector on each level, a working carbon monoxide detector within 10 feet of bedrooms, and an ABC extinguisher of 2 to 10 pounds within 10 feet of the kitchen.

faqs.q: Where in Englewood do I start the CCO process?
faqs.a: At the Building Department, second floor of the Municipal Building, 2-10 North Van Brunt Street. Have the buyer's name, phone and address ready, and close out any open permits first.

faqs.q: What happens if the inspector finds an illegal unit?
faqs.a: The owner removes the unit, including its kitchen and bathroom and utility service, and a second inspection confirms it before the certificate issues.
